translations.answer: ASE learns a reusable latent skill embedding from an unstructured motion collection and substantially simplifies several downstream simulated tasks. Its subject is a 37-DoF sword-and-shield simulated character, pretraining takes roughly ten days, and there is no robot-hardware experiment; it is a motion-prior baseline, not a ready-to-deploy physical controller.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The downstream task distribution can be covered by combinations of skills represented in the pretraining motion data.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Sufficient compute is available to train the adversarial skill prior and a stable high-level policy.
translations.applicability.controllers.0: Adversarial Skill Embeddings (ASE) and a hierarchical high-level policy
translations.applicability.environments.0: Simulated navigation, attack, and recovery tasks for a sword-and-shield character
translations.applicability.robots.0: A 37-DoF simulated character; no physical-robot evidence
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper reports multi-task, ablation, and recovery experiments, and the official code exposes skill encoding and high-level training. All results use a simulated character, pretraining costs about ten days, and hardware transfer is not demonstrated.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Sections 3-6, Figures 2-12, Tables 1-2, and the appendix
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines adversarial skill embeddings, the latent prior, and high-level task training, then reports multiple simulation experiments.
translations.evidence.0.title: ASE: Large-Scale Reusable Adversarial Skill Embeddings for Physically Simulated Characters
translations.terms.0: Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU, 惯性测量单元)
translations.title: Has ASE proved that its reusable skill embedding can directly serve as a general motion generator for physical humanoid robots?
